title: Antimetabolites in clinical oncology: folate antagonists, pyrimidine analogues and toxicity rescue

steps.tx: Folate analogues block single-carbon transfer reactions indispensable for de novo purine and thymidylate biosynthesis. **Methotrexate** competitively inhibits **dihydrofolate reductase** DHFR, depleting intracellular tetrahydrofolate and arresting cellular proliferation. High-dose methotrexate infusions require vigorous sodium bicarbonate urinary alkalinisation to maintain pH at or above 7.0, preventing tubular crystal precipitation.
steps.say: Folate analogues block single-carbon transfer reactions indispensable for de novo purine and thymidylate biosynthesis. Methotrexate competitively inhibits dihydrofolate reductase DHFR, depleting intracellular tetrahydrofolate and arresting cellular proliferation. High-dose methotrexate infusions require sodium bicarbonate alkalinisation to maintain pH above 7.0, preventing renal crystal precipitation.

steps.tx: The model shows **methotrexate** sitting in the active cleft of **dihydrofolate reductase** beside its NADPH cofactor. By blocking conversion of dihydrofolate to **tetrahydrofolate**, the drug starves cells of single carbon units needed for **purine** and thymidylate building. Without those blocks, DNA synthesis halts and dividing cells stop growing.
steps.say: Methotrexate fits tightly into the pocket of dihydrofolate reductase, the enzyme that normally refreshes folate for DNA building. With the pocket occupied, the cell cannot make tetrahydrofolate, so purine and thymidylate supplies fall and replication stalls. That is why the drug works against fast growing cancers and why healthy marrow and gut lining also suffer. High doses need alkalinised urine and leucovorin rescue to protect normal tissue.

vis.alt: A molecular model shows methotrexate occupying the active site of dihydrofolate reductase.
vis.caption: Methotrexate blocks folate recycling at the enzyme active site. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Systemic mucosal and marrow rescue is achieved by direct pharmacological bypass of dihydrofolate reductase. **Leucovorin** calcium **folinic acid** bypasses dihydrofolate reductase inhibition, supplying reduced tetrahydrofolate directly to normal host tissues. Administered every 6 hours following high-dose methotrexate, leucovorin rescues non-malignant marrow and mucosal tissues until serum methotrexate falls safely below 0.05 micromolar.

left.title: Leucovorin Rescue
points: Enters cells via reduced folate carrier
Rescues normal marrow and gastrointestinal mucosa

right.title: Folic Acid Ineffectiveness
points: Requires DHFR reduction to enter active folate pool
Used only for routine nutritional maintenance

steps.tx: Pyrimidine synthesis inhibition requires specific intracellular metabolic activation. **5-Fluorouracil** is converted to FdUMP, which forms an inactive ternary complex with **thymidylate synthase** and 5,10-methylene-tetrahydrofolate. This stable ternary complex blocks deoxythymidine monophosphate production, arresting DNA replication. Concurrent administration of leucovorin stabilises this complex, significantly augmenting 5-fluorouracil cytotoxic efficacy in gastrointestinal malignancies.
steps.say: Pyrimidine synthesis inhibition requires specific intracellular metabolic activation. 5-Fluorouracil is converted to FdUMP, which forms an inactive ternary complex with thymidylate synthase and methylene-tetrahydrofolate. This stable ternary complex blocks deoxythymidine monophosphate production, arresting DNA replication. Leucovorin stabilises this complex, augmenting 5-fluorouracil cytotoxic efficacy.

steps.tx: Oral fluoropyrimidine prodrugs exploit differential tumour enzyme expression for selective activation. **Capecitabine** is an orally absorbed fluoropyrimidine carbamate converted into 5-FU sequentially by hepatic carboxylesterase, cytidine deaminase, and intratumoral **thymidine phosphorylase**. Because thymidine phosphorylase is overexpressed in neoplastic tissues, capecitabine generates higher active fluorouracil concentrations inside solid tumours compared to adjacent healthy tissues.
steps.say: Oral fluoropyrimidine prodrugs exploit differential tumour enzyme expression for selective activation. Capecitabine is an orally absorbed fluoropyrimidine carbamate converted into 5-FU sequentially by hepatic carboxylesterase, cytidine deaminase, and intratumoral thymidine phosphorylase. Because thymidine phosphorylase is overexpressed in neoplastic tissues, capecitabine generates higher 5-FU concentrations inside tumours.

steps.tx: Nucleoside analogues disrupt nucleic acid chain elongation and pool maintenance. **Gemcitabine** is a deoxycytidine analogue that undergoes intracellular phosphorylation to diphosphate and triphosphate forms, inhibiting **ribonucleotide reductase** and incorporating into replicating DNA. Ribonucleotide reductase inhibition depletes endogenous deoxyribonucleotide pools, which self-potentiates gemcitabine triphosphate incorporation into DNA, terminating nascent chain synthesis.

steps.tx: Multitargeted antifolates inhibit multiple sequential enzymes across one-carbon metabolic pathways. **Pemetrexed** is a multi-targeted **antifolate** that potently inhibits thymidylate synthase, dihydrofolate reductase, and glycinamide ribonucleotide formyltransferase. Clinical administration mandates mandatory pre-treatment supplementation with daily oral folic acid and intramuscular vitamin B12 to prevent life-threatening haematologic and cutaneous toxicity in non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer.

left.title: Pemetrexed Target Profile
points: Active in non-squamous NSCLC and mesothelioma

right.title: Mandatory Pre-Medication
points: Oral folic acid (350 to 1000 mcg daily)

steps.tx: Deoxycytidine analogues require vigilant neurological surveillance during high-dose induction regimens. **Cytarabine** ara-C is incorporated into DNA as an antimetabolite, terminating chain elongation during S phase. High-dose cytarabine regimens exceed clearance capacity of cytidine deaminase in the central nervous system; high-dose therapy requires serial neurological examinations to detect irreversible **cerebellar toxicity**, manifesting as dysarthria, nystagmus, and dysmetria.

steps.tx: **Fluorouracil** toxicity is largely determined by **dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase** (DPD) activity. Patients with DPD deficiency need genotype or phenotype testing before treatment, and full dosing can be fatal. Severe diarrhoea requires withholding until it resolves, then dose reduction. Hand-foot syndrome is managed by grade, with dose reduction after recovery. Regular blood counts are mandatory during treatment.
steps.say: Fluorouracil toxicity is largely determined by dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase activity. Patients with DPD deficiency should be tested before treatment, because full dosing can be fatal. Severe diarrhoea requires withholding fluorouracil until it resolves, followed by dose reduction. Hand-foot syndrome is managed by grade, with dose reduction after recovery. Regular blood counts are mandatory throughout treatment to detect myelosuppression early.

steps.tx: Halogenated purine analogues induce profound immune suppression through lymphocyte ablation. **Fludarabine** and **cladribine** are **purine nucleoside** analogues causing profound, protracted **CD4 T-lymphocyte** depletion that persists for months to years post-treatment. This profound lymphopenia creates high susceptibility to opportunistic pathogens, requiring routine trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prophylaxis against Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and irradiated blood products to prevent fatal transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease.
